newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's North in A$19.5 mln iron ore study.
newsitem.headline: Australia's North in A$19.5 mln iron ore study.

text.p: North Ltd unit Robe River Iron Associates will commit A$19.5 million for a feasibility study into the potential development of rich iron ore deposits at West Angelas in the Pilbara region of Western Australia, North Ltd said in a statement.
Robe River Iron Associates' parent partners are the Australian resources company North Ltd, the Mitsui group of companies, Nippon Steel Australia Pty Ltd and Sumitomo Metal Australia Pty Ltd.
North Ltd deputy managing director Malcolm Broomhead said the West Angelas development was dependent on success of the feasibility study, regulatory and Native Title approvals and future markets.

About 100 km west of Newman and about 100 km east of Parabadoo in the northwest of Western Australia, West Angelas A and B orebodies have a mineable reserve of about 540 million tonnes at 61.5 percent iron, North said.
The feasibility study will include additional diamond and reserve circulation drilling, water supply exploration, bulk sampling of the orebody and mine planning and design, the statement said.
In addition there will be engineering, marketing and financial evaluatuion activities to support the full feasibility study, it said.

North Ltd said in January that it was keen to proceed to a full feasibility study on a new iron ore project in Australia's northwest and estimated that the deposit could cost up to A$1 billion to develop.
